question.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=3\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{6})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by the expression

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $3\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{6}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{6}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{6}=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{6} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =3\pi +6n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x=3\pi +6n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.
